title: VehicleState
description: Canonical vehicle state as consumed by MyRoboTaxi SDKs. Defines every field name, type, unit, nullability, atomic group membership, and data classification. Both the WebSocket vehicle_update messages and the REST snapshot endpoint return subsets of this schema. WHO SEES THIS SNAPSHOT, REWRITTEN BY MYR-602 (contracts v0.41.0). THE RULE: A NON-OWNER SEES THE CAR'S LIVE LOCATION ONLY DURING AN ACTIVE RIDE OR AN ACTIVE TRIP. That produces THREE NON-OWNER MASK ROLES, each a superset of the one before, with the STRONGEST APPLICABLE ROLE WINNING for a given (person, vehicle, instant). `viewer` — an accepted share and nothing else (MYR-184): the catalog and status fields, and NEITHER the LOCATION GROUP (`latitude`, `longitude`, `heading`, `speed`, `locationName`, `locationAddress`) NOR the NAVIGATION GROUP (`destinationName`, `destinationAddress`, `destinationLatitude`, `destinationLongitude`, `originLatitude`, `originLongitude`, `etaMinutes`, `tripDistanceRemaining`, `navRouteCoordinates`). `ride_member` — a party to an accepted, LIVE ride on this vehicle (MYR-540): viewer PLUS both groups, for the life of that ride. `trip_participant` — a non-left participant of an ACTIVE trip on this vehicle (MYR-602, trip.schema.json): IDENTICAL to `ride_member`, field for field, for the length of the trip's window and at ALL times inside it — parked, driving, with a destination or without one. THIS SUPERSEDES MYR-435, which kept the navigation group visible to plain viewers; MYR-602 withdraws it along with position. THE THREE ROLES ARE THE SERVER-SIDE MASK MODEL AND ARE NOT WIRE VALUES — `VehicleSummary.role` stays exactly `owner | viewer` and is NOT widened, because installed builds switch on it; a client learns it holds the stronger access from an accepted live ride it is party to, or from a non-null `VehicleSummary.activeTripId`. HOW THE NARROWING REACHES THE WIRE: the six location-group fields are in this schema's `required` set, so the plain-viewer projection emits each one's DOCUMENTED NO-VALUE SENTINEL rather than dropping the key — `latitude`/`longitude` as 0,0 (the '0,0 = no fix' convention, §2.3), `locationName`/`locationAddress` as '' (the 'no geocode yet' convention), and `speed`/`heading` as 0 — because omitting a required key would mint a frame this package calls invalid, and truly relaxing `required` is major-bump territory. The navigation fields are all nullable and are simply null, which the `navigation` group already defines as 'no active navigation'. ONE HONEST CONSEQUENCE: `speed: 0` and `heading: 0` are REAL readings for a stopped car pointing north, so a consumer MUST decide what to draw from THE ROLE IT HOLDS, never by sniffing the values. The authoritative role/mask table lives in the telemetry repo's `docs/contracts/rest-api.md` §5 and `docs/contracts/data-classification.md`.

vehicleId.description: Opaque database identifier (cuid). NOT the VIN. All SDK API calls use this ID (FR-4.2).

name.description: User-assigned vehicle name from DB Vehicle.name (managed by the Next.js settings UI). NOT the Tesla-streamed VehicleName proto field — see vehicle-state-schema.md §1.2 for the disambiguation rationale (MYR-30).

model.description: Vehicle model (e.g., 'Model 3', 'Model Y'). Sourced from DB Vehicle.model (Prisma NOT NULL). Loaded by the Go Vehicle struct and populated on snapshot as of MYR-24 (2026-04-23).

year.description: Model year. Sourced from DB Vehicle.year (Prisma NOT NULL). Loaded by the Go Vehicle struct and populated on snapshot as of MYR-24 (2026-04-23).

color.description: Vehicle exterior color. Sourced from DB Vehicle.color (Prisma NOT NULL). Loaded by the Go Vehicle struct and populated on snapshot as of MYR-24 (2026-04-23).

vin.description: Full 17-character Vehicle Identification Number, sourced from DB Vehicle.vin. **Owner-snapshot only (MYR-279):** returned on the REST /snapshot to the vehicle's OWNER, gated to the owner role mask (party-scoped) -- a shared viewer does NOT receive it (removed from the viewer allow-list) and it is NEVER emitted on the WebSocket vehicle_update broadcast. The vehicles-list catalog (vehicle-summary.schema.json) surfaces vinLast4 only. Classified P0 (a VIN is publicly stamped on the car) but MUST be redacted to ***XXXX in all logs because it links to location data (P1) -- see data-classification.md section 1.3 / section 2.1. Optional: not a member of the required set, so older snapshot consumers are unaffected.

softwareVersion.description: Installed Tesla firmware version string (e.g. '2026.20.1 9a8b7c6'). Sourced from the streamed Tesla proto Version field OR REST vehicle_data.vehicle_state.car_version (the MYR-260 /vehicle_data backfill for a non-streaming car). MYR-279: persisted server-side to the Go-owned go_vehicle_control_state side table (keyed by vehicle id, no Prisma FK per CG-DL-9; migration 0011) and returned on the DB-backed REST /snapshot (LEFT-joined by VehicleRepo.GetByID). Null when never read. Individually delivered -- not a member of any atomic group.

trim.description: Vehicle trim badge (e.g. 'Performance', 'Long Range'). Sourced ONLY from REST vehicle_data.vehicle_config.trim_badging -- Tesla does NOT stream the trim, so it is plucked by the MYR-260 /vehicle_data backfill. MYR-279: persisted to the Go-owned go_vehicle_control_state side table (migration 0011) and returned on the DB-backed REST /snapshot (LEFT-joined by VehicleRepo.GetByID). Null when never read (e.g. a car that has only ever streamed and never had a /vehicle_data backfill). Lets the client compose a full model label like '2026 Model Y Performance'.

status.description: Derived vehicle status. Part of the gear atomic group -- updated atomically with gearPosition. When gearPosition is D or R, status is 'driving' (driving outranks every other state); otherwise 'in_service' when a service signal is set, else 'parked'. The 'in_service' state (MYR-259) is set when the pushed ServiceMode field (Tesla proto 159) is on OR Tesla's REST in_service bool is true, and outranks parked/charging/offline. The 'charging' and 'offline' states are set by other server-side logic. See vehicle-state-schema.md section 2.4.

speed.description: Current vehicle speed. Rounded to nearest integer from Tesla's float emission. MYR-602 VISIBILITY (contracts v0.41.0): part of the LOCATION GROUP, which a NON-OWNER receives only during an active ride (`ride_member`) or an active trip (`trip_participant`). A plain `viewer` — an accepted share with neither — receives this field's documented no-value sentinel instead of a reading; see this schema's root description for the sentinel per field and for why the key is not dropped.

heading.description: Compass heading. 0 = North, 90 = East, 180 = South, 270 = West. Per the '0,0 = no fix' convention (§2.3), SDK consumers MUST treat latitude == 0 && longitude == 0 as 'no position available' rather than a valid location in the Gulf of Guinea. gearPosition.description: Transmission gear position. Null when vehicle is asleep or gear has not yet been reported. When gearPosition changes, status is re-derived and both are delivered together.

chargeLevel.description: Battery state of charge. Rounded to nearest integer from Tesla's float emission. Maps from Tesla SOC or BatteryLevel fields.

chargeState.description: Charge state enum sourced from Tesla proto field 179 (DetailedChargeState) as of MYR-42 (2026-04-23). Added as a v1 charge atomic group member by MYR-11; live WS wiring completed by MYR-40 on 2026-04-22 using proto 2 (ChargeState); re-sourced to proto 179 by MYR-42 after empirical capture showed Tesla firmware ≥ 2024.44.25 accepts proto 2 in fleet_telemetry_config but never actually emits it. Proto 179 fires on the same transitions with identical enum string values (see websocket-protocol.md §4.1.4 and §10 DV-03 + DV-19). DB persistence on the Prisma-owned Vehicle table landed in MYR-41 on 2026-04-25 (Vehicle.chargeState String? + Go writer pipeline applier + store SELECT/UPDATE wiring). Nullable in steady state — a vehicle that has never charged surfaces null on both wire and REST /snapshot. SDK consumers MUST tolerate null and render a neutral placeholder (not a spinner). Nullability is expressed via the union `type: ["string", "null"]`; the `enum` list includes `null` explicitly alongside the string values for maximum validator compatibility (some Go and Python JSON Schema libraries require `null` in the enum to accept null values even when `type` includes `null`).

estimatedRange.description: Estimated remaining driving range based on current charge. Rounded to nearest integer.

timeToFull.description: Estimated time to full charge at the current charging rate. Added as a v1 charge atomic group member by MYR-11; live WS wiring completed by MYR-40 on 2026-04-22 (see websocket-protocol.md §4.1.4 and §10 DV-04). Tesla proto field 43 (TimeToFullCharge, double). Unit is HOURS (decimal, fractional values supported — e.g. 1.5 for 90 minutes) per the tesla-fleet-telemetry-sme skill and the legacy Tesla REST API; empirically verified as 1.066666841506958 hours during a home charging session on 2026-04-22 (DV-17 resolved — see MYR-25 comment and TestDecoder_DecodePayload_TimeToFull). DB persistence on the Prisma-owned Vehicle table landed in MYR-41 on 2026-04-25 (Vehicle.timeToFull Float? + Go writer pipeline applier + store SELECT/UPDATE wiring). Nullable in steady state — null means no active charging session or no charge frame has arrived yet. SDK consumers MUST tolerate null and render a neutral placeholder (not a spinner). 0 (or null when disconnected) means no active charging session.

interiorTemp.description: Cabin interior temperature. Rounded to nearest integer. OWNER-ONLY since MYR-435 (client decision 2026-08-02: remove cabin state from viewers) — cabin temperature is a live occupancy signal. Moved OUT of `required` in the same change: a field the viewer mask omits MUST be optional here, or every viewer document fails its own schema.

exteriorTemp.description: Ambient exterior temperature. Rounded to nearest integer. OWNER-ONLY since MYR-435 — the ambiguous case, resolved toward removal: ambient air is closer to weather than to privacy, but a rider beside the car already knows the weather, no viewer-facing surface renders it, and it arrives on the same climate read-back as its cabin siblings, so for a viewer it is data with no consumer. NOTE: it is NOT a member of any declared x-atomic-group (an earlier draft of this description said otherwise), so withholding it splits no group — the guard is TestViewerMaskNeverSplitsAnAtomicGroup. Moved OUT of `required` in the same change, for the same reason as interiorTemp.

odometerMiles.description: Total odometer reading. Rounded to nearest integer.

fsdMilesSinceReset.description: Miles driven using Full Self-Driving since last reset. The counter resets on OTA updates and factory resets, NOT daily. Maps from Tesla SelfDrivingMilesSinceReset. Non-nullable per DB Vehicle.fsdMilesSinceReset (NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) — DB column renamed from the legacy fsdMilesToday by MYR-24 (2026-04-23, cross-repo Prisma migration). Loaded by the Go Vehicle struct and populated on snapshot.

locked.description: Whether the vehicle is locked. Sourced from Tesla proto field 59 (Locked, boolean). Added by MYR-252 as an owner cabin-control read-back field. Delivered live on the WebSocket vehicle_update stream (individually-delivered field, no atomic group); the value is absent from a frame until the vehicle emits a change. **MYR-269 (NFR-3.5 hydration):** now persisted server-side to the Go-owned `go_vehicle_control_state` side table (keyed by vehicle id, no Prisma FK per CG-DL-9) whenever it arrives — live stream OR the MYR-260 `/vehicle_data` backfill — and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` (LEFT-joined by `VehicleRepo.GetByID`), so a non-streaming car (in service / asleep / offline) surfaces the last-known value with no live socket instead of a perpetual "unavailable". Null when never read.

hvacPower.description: Climate (HVAC) system power state. Sourced from Tesla proto field 201 (HvacPower, HvacPowerState enum). Added by MYR-252. Live WS vehicle_update field. MYR-269: the `hvacPower` enum string itself stays WS-only, but its server-derived `isClimateOn` boolean is now persisted and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` for non-streaming cars.

isClimateOn.description: Convenience boolean derived server-side from `hvacPower`: false when hvacPower is 'Off', true when it is 'On'/'Precondition'/'OverheatProtect'. When hvacPower is 'Unknown' this field is OMITTED entirely (not sent as any value) so the client renders an honest 'unknown' rather than a fabricated on/off state (MYR-251/252). Added by MYR-252 so consumers can render a climate on/off toggle without interpreting the HvacPowerState enum. Derived from Tesla proto field 201; no dedicated proto field. **MYR-269 (NFR-3.5 hydration):** now persisted server-side to the Go-owned `go_vehicle_control_state` side table (keyed by vehicle id, no Prisma FK per CG-DL-9) whenever it arrives — live stream OR the MYR-260 `/vehicle_data` backfill — and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` (LEFT-joined by `VehicleRepo.GetByID`), so a non-streaming car (in service / asleep / offline) surfaces the last-known value with no live socket instead of a perpetual "unavailable". Null when never read.

Live WS vehicle_update field. **MYR-273 (NFR-3.5 hydration):** now persisted server-side to the Go-owned `go_vehicle_control_state` side table (keyed by vehicle id, no Prisma FK per CG-DL-9) whenever it arrives — live stream OR the MYR-260 `/vehicle_data` backfill — and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` (LEFT-joined by `VehicleRepo.GetByID`), so a non-streaming car (in service / asleep / offline) surfaces the last-known value with no live socket instead of a perpetual unavailable placeholder. Null when never read.

seatVentEnabled.description: Whether seat ventilation is enabled. Sourced from Tesla proto field 254 (SeatVentEnabled, boolean). Added by MYR-252 (Group B). Live WS vehicle_update field. **MYR-298 (NFR-3.5 hydration):** now persisted server-side to the Go-owned `go_vehicle_control_state` side table (migration 0014, `seat_vent_enabled BOOLEAN`; no Prisma FK per CG-DL-9) on the live stream path and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` (LEFT-joined by `VehicleRepo.GetByID`), so a client that missed the live frame can still learn it. A real `false` is an observation and overwrites; null when never read. NOT written by the MYR-260 `/vehicle_data` backfill — Tesla's cached vehicle_data subset does not carry it.

seatCoolingCapable.description: Whether this vehicle is EQUIPPED WITH ventilated (cooled) front seats. A SPEC/CAPABILITY fact about the car, NOT a runtime state — contrast the sibling `seatVentEnabled` (Tesla proto 254), which is the runtime on/off of that equipment. A car can be `seatCoolingCapable: true` with `seatVentEnabled: false` (equipped, currently off), and a car that is `seatCoolingCapable: false` can never report `seatVentEnabled: true`. Sourced ONLY from Tesla REST `vehicle_data.vehicle_config.has_seat_cooling`, read by the server's vehicle-config read (MYR-308) — Tesla does NOT stream this, there is no proto field for it, and it therefore carries NO live WebSocket delta: a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER contains seatCoolingCapable. It arrives on REST reads only (this `/snapshot` and the vehicles-list row), like the sibling `trim`, which is likewise plucked from `vehicle_config`. OPTIONAL: ABSENT (or null) means the server predates MYR-308 or has never completed a vehicle-config read for this car; it does NOT mean 'no seat cooling'. On absent, clients MUST fall back to the existing telemetry-presence heuristic — treat the car as seat-cooling-capable if `seatCoolerLeft`/`seatCoolerRight` have ever been non-null — rather than hiding the control outright. An explicit `false`, by contrast, is AUTHORITATIVE and OUTRANKS that heuristic: the car has no ventilated seats and clients MUST NOT offer seat-cooling controls (no greyed-out row, no disabled slider that implies the hardware exists). Classified P0: an equipment/trim fact about the vehicle, not identifying data and not user content — the same tier as `trim`, `model` and `year`.

chargePortDoorOpen.description: Whether the charge-port door is open. Sourced from Tesla proto field 183 (ChargePortDoorOpen, boolean). Added by MYR-252 (Group B). Individually-delivered — intentionally NOT a member of the `charge` atomic group (it is a door state, not a battery/charge-session value). Live WS vehicle_update field. **MYR-269 (NFR-3.5 hydration):** now persisted server-side to the Go-owned `go_vehicle_control_state` side table (keyed by vehicle id, no Prisma FK per CG-DL-9) whenever it arrives — live stream OR the MYR-260 `/vehicle_data` backfill — and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` (LEFT-joined by `VehicleRepo.GetByID`), so a non-streaming car (in service / asleep / offline) surfaces the last-known value with no live socket instead of a perpetual "unavailable". Null when never read.

frunkOpen.description: Whether the front trunk (frunk) is open. Decoded from Tesla proto field 58 (DoorState) — the `Doors` message's TrunkFront boolean. Added by MYR-252 (Group B). See vehicle-state-schema.md §6.1 for the DoorState bit decode. Live WS vehicle_update field. **MYR-269 (NFR-3.5 hydration):** now persisted server-side to the Go-owned `go_vehicle_control_state` side table (keyed by vehicle id, no Prisma FK per CG-DL-9) whenever it arrives — live stream OR the MYR-260 `/vehicle_data` backfill — and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` (LEFT-joined by `VehicleRepo.GetByID`), so a non-streaming car (in service / asleep / offline) surfaces the last-known value with no live socket instead of a perpetual "unavailable". Null when never read.

trunkOpen.description: Whether the rear trunk is open. Decoded from Tesla proto field 58 (DoorState) — the `Doors` message's TrunkRear boolean. Added by MYR-252 (Group B). See vehicle-state-schema.md §6.1 for the DoorState bit decode. Live WS vehicle_update field. **MYR-269 (NFR-3.5 hydration):** now persisted server-side to the Go-owned `go_vehicle_control_state` side table (keyed by vehicle id, no Prisma FK per CG-DL-9) whenever it arrives — live stream OR the MYR-260 `/vehicle_data` backfill — and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` (LEFT-joined by `VehicleRepo.GetByID`), so a non-streaming car (in service / asleep / offline) surfaces the last-known value with no live socket instead of a perpetual "unavailable". Null when never read.

mediaPlaybackStatus.description: Media playback status. Sourced from Tesla proto field 242 (MediaPlaybackStatus, MediaStatus enum). Added by MYR-252 (Group B). Live WS vehicle_update field. **MYR-298 (NFR-3.5 hydration):** now persisted server-side to the Go-owned `go_vehicle_control_state` side table (migration 0014, `media_playback_status TEXT` holding the enum's string form; no Prisma FK per CG-DL-9) on the live stream path and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` (LEFT-joined by `VehicleRepo.GetByID`), so a client that missed the live frame can still learn it. Honest-unknown is preserved: a streamed "Unknown"/empty is OMITTED (persists NULL, never overwrites a known status), mirroring how an "Unknown" hvacAutoMode is omitted — so the persisted value is only ever Stopped/Playing/Paused, and null when never read. NOT written by the MYR-260 `/vehicle_data` backfill — Tesla's cached vehicle_data subset does not carry it.

mediaVolume.description: Current media audio volume. Sourced from Tesla proto field 244 (MediaAudioVolume). Tesla emits a fractional level (typically 0-11), so this is a number (not integer-rounded). Added by MYR-252 (Group B). Live WS vehicle_update field. **MYR-273 (NFR-3.5 hydration):** now persisted server-side to the Go-owned `go_vehicle_control_state` side table as a nullable DOUBLE PRECISION column (keyed by vehicle id, no Prisma FK per CG-DL-9) whenever it arrives — live stream OR the MYR-260 `/vehicle_data` backfill — and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` (LEFT-joined by `VehicleRepo.GetByID`), so a non-streaming car (in service / asleep / offline) surfaces the last-known value with no live socket instead of a perpetual unavailable placeholder. Null when never read.

licensePlate.description: Owner-entered license plate for this vehicle. NOT sourced from Tesla — the Fleet API exposes no plate on any endpoint, telemetry field, or proto, so this value exists only because the vehicle's owner typed it: it is set and cleared via `PUT /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/plate` (MYR-286) and persisted server-side. The server NORMALIZES on write — uppercased, leading/trailing whitespace trimmed, at most 10 characters, and restricted to the charset A-Z, 0-9, space, and hyphen; submitting an empty string to that PUT CLEARS the stored plate. Reads therefore only ever return an already-normalized value, so consumers MUST NOT re-normalize or re-validate before display. OPTIONAL and deliberately tolerant: ABSENT and EMPTY STRING both mean 'no plate set' (an absent field additionally means the server may predate MYR-286) — neither ever means 'this car has a plate we could not read'. Consumers MUST keep their existing `VIN ····xxxx` fallback label for both cases and MUST NEVER render an empty plate (no blank chip, no stray separator, no 'Plate: ' with nothing after it). Visibility is deliberately BOTH ROLES: owner AND viewer/rider receive this field, unlike the sibling `vin`, which MYR-279 gated to the owner role mask. That asymmetry is an intentional product decision, not an oversight — the entire purpose of the plate is that a rider can identify the correct car at pickup, which fails if only the owner can see it. Classified P1 rather than P0 (unlike `model`/`color`) precisely because of that reach: a plate is externally correlatable to a person via DMV and third-party registry lookups, so it is identifying data — redact it in logs and never emit it outside the vehicle's party (owner plus invited viewers/riders of that vehicle). Delivery: v1 carries NO live WebSocket delta for this field — a vehicle_update frame NEVER contains licensePlate, and a plate edit fires no push. It changes only through the PUT above and reaches clients on the next read: this REST /snapshot and the GET /api/vehicles list row (vehicle-summary.schema.json). A client that needs the new value immediately after an edit re-reads (or optimistically applies its own PUT response) rather than waiting for a stream update.

mediaNowPlayingTitle.description: Title of the track currently playing in the vehicle. Sourced from Tesla proto field 248 (MediaNowPlayingTitle). Added by MYR-303 as a sibling of the MYR-252 media read-backs `mediaPlaybackStatus`/`mediaVolume`. Delivery: streamed live on the WebSocket `vehicle_update` stream (Tesla fleet-telemetry **Media** group, pushed ON CHANGE — the car emits a frame when the track changes; there is no polling and no fixed interval), then persisted server-side on arrival and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` exactly like the sibling cabin read-backs (MYR-269/MYR-273 `go_vehicle_control_state` hydration), so a non-streaming car (asleep, in service, offline) surfaces the last-known now-playing block instead of an empty panel. OPTIONAL: ABSENT (or null) means this field has NEVER been observed for this vehicle — the car has not streamed a title since the server started recording one, or the server predates MYR-303. It NEVER means 'something is playing whose title we could not read', and consumers MUST render their honest empty/unknown state rather than a placeholder track (the fixture leak MYR-264 removed). Free text from Tesla — arbitrary length, any script, no normalization; consumers MUST truncate for display rather than assume a bound. Classified **P1**, deliberately stricter than the P0 sibling `mediaPlaybackStatus`/`mediaVolume`: this is free-text USER CONTENT, and an accumulated title/artist/album/station stream reveals listening habits (taste, and by inference language, mood, politics, religion). Handling: REDACT IN LOGS — never log the value, log only presence/length. Visibility is BOTH ROLES, owner AND viewer/rider of this vehicle, which is the whole point of the feature (a rider sees what the car is playing); that is fine and intended. What is NOT fine: emitting it outside the vehicle's party, aggregating it, or retaining it as a listening history.

mediaNowPlayingArtist.description: Artist of the track currently playing in the vehicle. Sourced from Tesla proto field 247 (MediaNowPlayingArtist). Added by MYR-303 as a sibling of the MYR-252 media read-backs `mediaPlaybackStatus`/`mediaVolume`. Delivery: streamed live on the WebSocket `vehicle_update` stream (Tesla fleet-telemetry **Media** group, pushed ON CHANGE — no polling), then persisted server-side on arrival and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` exactly like the sibling cabin read-backs, so a non-streaming car surfaces the last-known value with no live socket. OPTIONAL: ABSENT (or null) means NEVER OBSERVED — not 'unreadable', and never a reason to render a placeholder. Present independently of `mediaNowPlayingTitle`: the two are individually-delivered fields with NO atomic group and NO dependentRequired pairing, so a frame may carry one without the other and consumers MUST render each half honestly rather than blanking the block when only one arrives. Free text from Tesla — arbitrary length, any script, no normalization. Classified **P1** for the same reason as `mediaNowPlayingTitle`: free-text user content whose accumulation reveals listening habits. REDACT IN LOGS (presence/length only). Visibility is BOTH ROLES — owner AND viewer/rider of this vehicle — which is intended; it MUST NOT leave the vehicle's party or be retained as a listening history.

mediaNowPlayingAlbum.description: Album of the track currently playing in the vehicle. Sourced from Tesla proto field 249 (MediaNowPlayingAlbum). Added by MYR-303 as a sibling of the MYR-252 media read-backs `mediaPlaybackStatus`/`mediaVolume`. Delivery: streamed live on the WebSocket `vehicle_update` stream (Tesla fleet-telemetry **Media** group, pushed ON CHANGE — no polling), then persisted server-side on arrival and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` exactly like the sibling cabin read-backs. OPTIONAL: ABSENT (or null) means NEVER OBSERVED. Expect this field to be absent far more often than `mediaNowPlayingTitle`/`mediaNowPlayingArtist` — radio and many streaming sources carry no album at all — so it is a SECONDARY display line that consumers MUST be able to omit without leaving a gap in the layout. Free text from Tesla — arbitrary length, any script, no normalization. Classified **P1** for the same reason as `mediaNowPlayingTitle`: free-text user content whose accumulation reveals listening habits. REDACT IN LOGS (presence/length only). Visibility is BOTH ROLES — owner AND viewer/rider of this vehicle — which is intended; it MUST NOT leave the vehicle's party or be retained as a listening history.

mediaNowPlayingStation.description: The STATION playing media — the radio/streaming source label the car shows above the track, e.g. a satellite-radio channel, an FM/AM station name, or a streaming service's station/playlist label. Sourced from Tesla proto field 250 (MediaNowPlayingStation). Distinct from the sibling `mediaPlaybackSource`, which names the INPUT doing the playing (the app or connection); a frame may carry either, both, or neither. Added by MYR-303 as a sibling of the MYR-252 media read-backs `mediaPlaybackStatus`/`mediaVolume`. Delivery: streamed live on the WebSocket `vehicle_update` stream (Tesla fleet-telemetry **Media** group, pushed ON CHANGE — no polling), then persisted server-side on arrival and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` exactly like the sibling cabin read-backs. OPTIONAL: ABSENT (or null) means NEVER OBSERVED, not 'no station' and not 'unreadable'. Free text from Tesla — no enumerated value set, arbitrary length; consumers MUST treat it as an opaque display label and MUST NOT switch behavior on it. Classified **P1** for the same reason as `mediaNowPlayingTitle`: free-text user content, and a station in particular is a direct signal of taste and often of language, politics, or religion. REDACT IN LOGS (presence/length only). Visibility is BOTH ROLES — owner AND viewer/rider of this vehicle — which is intended; it MUST NOT leave the vehicle's party or be retained as a listening history.

mediaPlaybackSource.description: The SOURCE actively used for playing media — the app or input the car is playing from, e.g. a streaming app name, `Bluetooth`, `USB`, or a tuner. Sourced from Tesla proto field 243 (MediaPlaybackSource). Distinct from the sibling `mediaNowPlayingStation`, which is the station/channel label WITHIN a source. Added by MYR-303 as a sibling of the MYR-252 media read-backs `mediaPlaybackStatus`/`mediaVolume`. Delivery: streamed live on the WebSocket `vehicle_update` stream (Tesla fleet-telemetry **Media** group, pushed ON CHANGE — no polling), then persisted server-side on arrival and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` exactly like the sibling cabin read-backs. OPTIONAL: ABSENT (or null) means NEVER OBSERVED. Free text from Tesla and deliberately NOT modelled as an enum — Tesla documents no fixed value set, and the values vary by market, software version, and installed apps, so a closed enum would silently mis-decode. Consumers MUST treat it as an opaque display string: MUST NOT switch on it, MUST NOT map it to an icon set without an unknown fallback, and MUST NOT assume stable casing or spelling across firmware. Classified **P1** for the same reason as `mediaNowPlayingTitle`: free-text user content, and the set of sources a person plays from is itself a habits signal. REDACT IN LOGS (presence/length only). Visibility is BOTH ROLES — owner AND viewer/rider of this vehicle — which is intended; it MUST NOT leave the vehicle's party or be retained as a listening history.

mediaNowPlayingDurationMs.description: Total length of the currently-playing track, in MILLISECONDS. Sourced from Tesla proto field 245 (MediaNowPlayingDuration). Added by MYR-303 as a sibling of the MYR-252 media read-backs `mediaPlaybackStatus`/`mediaVolume`. **SENTINEL — 18000000:** Tesla reports 18000000 ms (5 hours) as a placeholder for RADIO STATIONS and other continuous sources that have no real track length. That value is NOT a five-hour track. Consumers MUST special-case it: treat 18000000 as 'no duration', render a live/continuous indicator instead of a time remaining, and DO NOT draw a progress bar or compute a completion percentage against it (pairing it with `mediaNowPlayingElapsedMs`, which is itself unreliable on radio, would render a scrubber that crawls from 0% and never moves). Delivery: streamed live on the WebSocket `vehicle_update` stream (Tesla fleet-telemetry **Media** group, pushed ON CHANGE — no polling), then persisted server-side on arrival and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` exactly like the sibling cabin read-backs. OPTIONAL: ABSENT (or null) means NEVER OBSERVED — distinct from the 18000000 sentinel, which means 'observed, and the source has no duration'. Classified P0 rather than P1: a track length is a bare number that identifies nothing on its own, consistent with the sibling `mediaVolume`. It nonetheless travels alongside the P1 `mediaNowPlayingTitle`/`Artist`/`Album`/`Station`/`mediaPlaybackSource` fields, so it MUST NOT be used to reconstruct or fingerprint a listening history.

mediaNowPlayingElapsedMs.description: Playback position within the currently-playing track, in MILLISECONDS. Sourced from Tesla proto field 246 (MediaNowPlayingElapsed). Added by MYR-303 as a sibling of the MYR-252 media read-backs `mediaPlaybackStatus`/`mediaVolume`. **RELIABILITY CAVEAT:** per Tesla's fleet-telemetry documentation this value MAY BE NONSENSICAL FOR RADIO STATIONS — on a continuous source it can exceed the reported `mediaNowPlayingDurationMs`, stall, or reset unpredictably. Consumers MUST clamp before use and MUST suppress the scrubber entirely when `mediaNowPlayingDurationMs` is absent or equal to its 18000000 radio sentinel, rather than rendering a position the car does not actually mean. Even on real tracks this is a SAMPLED value, not a ticking clock: it updates only when the car emits a Media frame, so a client that wants a smooth progress bar must interpolate locally from the last sample and re-sync on each frame. Delivery: streamed live on the WebSocket `vehicle_update` stream (Tesla fleet-telemetry **Media** group, pushed ON CHANGE — no polling), then persisted server-side on arrival and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` exactly like the sibling cabin read-backs; note that a persisted elapsed value is STALE BY CONSTRUCTION (it was the position at the last frame, not at read time), so a `/snapshot` consumer MUST NOT present it as a live position. OPTIONAL: ABSENT (or null) means NEVER OBSERVED. Classified P0 rather than P1: a playback offset identifies nothing on its own, consistent with the sibling `mediaVolume`. It nonetheless travels alongside the P1 free-text media fields, so it MUST NOT be used to reconstruct or fingerprint a listening history.

mediaVolumeMax.description: The MAXIMUM SELECTABLE volume for this vehicle — the upper bound of the sibling `mediaVolume`, in the same unitless Tesla volume level (typically 0-11, so this is typically 11). Sourced from Tesla proto field 252 (MediaAudioVolumeMax); the wire name contracts that proto name to `mediaVolumeMax` for consistency with the sibling `mediaVolume`, which contracts `MediaAudioVolume` (proto 244) the same way. A `number`, NOT an integer, deliberately mirroring `mediaVolume`, which MYR-252 kept fractional and excluded from the server's integer-rounding set. Added by MYR-303 as a sibling of the MYR-252 media read-backs `mediaPlaybackStatus`/`mediaVolume`. USE: consumers rendering a volume percentage or slider MUST compute against this value (`mediaVolume / mediaVolumeMax`) rather than hard-coding 11 — the ceiling is per-vehicle and can differ across models and firmware. When this field is absent, a consumer MAY fall back to 11 but MUST treat that as an assumption, not a contract. Delivery: streamed live on the WebSocket `vehicle_update` stream (Tesla fleet-telemetry **Media** group, pushed ON CHANGE — no polling; in practice this is near-constant per vehicle and changes far less often than `mediaVolume`), then persisted server-side on arrival and returned on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` exactly like the sibling cabin read-backs, so a non-streaming car can still scale its last-known volume correctly. OPTIONAL: ABSENT (or null) means NEVER OBSERVED. Classified P0, matching the sibling `mediaVolume` — a volume ceiling is a device capability, not user content or identifying data.

serviceEstimatedEndAt.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 UTC instant at which the vehicle's CURRENT SERVICE VISIT is estimated to END. Added by MYR-316. Meaningful only while the sibling `status` is 'in_service': owners render it as 'Estimated completion …' beneath the In Service status, and the rider scheduling flow uses it as a FLOOR on when a ride may be booked. SERVER-COMPUTED, never client-supplied on this shape, with a fixed SOURCE PRECEDENCE: (1) Tesla's own estimate, `service_data.service_etc` from the Fleet API `GET /api/1/vehicles/{vin}/service_data`, polled on connectivity edges while the vehicle is in service; (2) failing that, the OWNER-ENTERED 'expected back' value, set via `PUT /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/service-window` (MYR-316); (3) null when neither exists. Tesla returns an ALL-NULL service_data body for visits that have no appointment record, so an absent estimate is COMMON AND NORMAL — it is not an error, not a fetch failure, and not a claim that the car is back. CLEARED AUTOMATICALLY when the vehicle leaves 'in_service': a driving/parked/charging/offline vehicle never carries a non-null value, so consumers never need to age this field out themselves. CONSUMER RULES: the rider scheduling picker floors its selectable range at this instant plus a small buffer, and the server likewise REFUSES scheduled ride requests for a time before it; when the field is ABSENT or NULL there is NO BOUND and scheduling stays fully open — consumers MUST NEVER block or gate scheduling on missing data. Delivery: NOT STREAMED. This field is REST-derived and carries no live WebSocket delta — a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER contains serviceEstimatedEndAt — so it is SNAPSHOT-ONLY for the Kit merger and arrives on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot` and on `GET /api/vehicles` list rows. Classified P0: operational timing about the car, not identifying data and not user content — the same tier as the sibling `status`.

trimLabel.description: HUMAN-READABLE trim / performance designation for this vehicle (e.g. 'Performance'), suitable for DIRECT DISPLAY. Added by MYR-320. Sourced ONLY from Tesla REST `vehicle_data.vehicle_config.performance_package` — live-verified against the owner's own car (MYR-320), which reports 'Performance'. CONTRAST THE SIBLING `trim`: that field carries the RAW BADGE CODE from `vehicle_config.trim_badging` (e.g. 'p74d'), a wire-level identifier that is NOT display-safe. Both fields are kept and neither replaces the other — `trim` stays the unmodified badge code for downstream classification, trimLabel is the label a human reads — but trimLabel is the ONLY one of the two a consumer may render. CONSUMER RULES: compose the display model name as '<year> <model> <trimLabel>' — e.g. '2026 Model Y Performance' — and OMIT THE LABEL ENTIRELY, falling back to '<year> <model>', when trimLabel is absent or null; consumers MUST NOT substitute `trim` in its place, MUST NOT re-case or otherwise reformat the value (it arrives already display-ready), and MUST NEVER emit a dangling separator or trailing space for the absent case. Delivery: NOT STREAMED. This field is REST-derived and read on the SAME NON-WAKING connectivity-edge / periodic vehicle-config read that populates the sibling `trim` (MYR-279, MYR-320); Tesla exposes no proto field for it, so a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER contains trimLabel — it is SNAPSHOT-ONLY for the Kit merger and arrives on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot`. Deliberately a DETAIL-SHEET FIELD ONLY: it is NOT added to the vehicles-list row (vehicle-summary.schema.json). OPTIONAL: ABSENT (or null) means the server predates MYR-320 or has NOT YET COMPLETED a vehicle-config read for this car; a vehicle whose configuration carries no performance designation may also legitimately report nothing here. Absence is therefore COMMON AND NORMAL — it is not an error, not a fetch failure, and not a claim about which trim the car is. Classified P0: an equipment/trim fact about the car, not identifying data and not user content — the same tier as the siblings `trim`, `model` and `year`.

fsdVersion.description: The vehicle's CURRENT FSD SOFTWARE DESIGNATION, exactly as Tesla names it (e.g. 'FSD (Supervised) v14.3.5'). Added by MYR-320. Sourced ONLY from the TITLE of the NEWEST ENTRY returned by the Fleet API `GET /api/1/vehicles/{vin}/release_notes` — live-verified against the owner's own car (MYR-320), which returned exactly that title. NO `vehicle_data` FIELD CARRIES THIS: the release-notes title is the only source Tesla exposes, so it appears in no telemetry group and no vehicle_data payload. DISTINCT FROM the sibling `softwareVersion`, which is the INSTALLED FIRMWARE BUILD (e.g. '2026.20.1 9a8b7c6') — the two strings move independently and NEITHER CAN BE DERIVED FROM THE OTHER. FREE-FORM AND PASSED THROUGH VERBATIM: the shape of this string is Tesla's and may change (parenthetical qualifiers, the 'v' prefix, point-release depth), so consumers MUST render it as-is and MUST NOT parse it, compare it ordinally, or gate any feature on a version number extracted from it. CONSUMER RULE: owners render it as ITS OWN ROW in the vehicle details sheet; when the field is absent or null that row is OMITTED ENTIRELY — no 'Unknown', no empty row, no placeholder dash. Delivery: NOT STREAMED. REST-derived on the SAME NON-WAKING connectivity-edge / periodic read family as the siblings `trim` and `trimLabel` (MYR-320) — a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER contains fsdVersion — so it is SNAPSHOT-ONLY for the Kit merger and arrives on the DB-backed REST `/snapshot`. Deliberately a DETAIL-SHEET FIELD ONLY: it is NOT added to the vehicles-list row (vehicle-summary.schema.json). OPTIONAL: ABSENT (or null) means the server predates MYR-320 or has not yet completed a release-notes read for this car; it does NOT mean the vehicle lacks FSD and it is NOT an error. Classified P0: a software designation of the car, the same tier as the sibling `softwareVersion` — not identifying data and not user content.

rideShareEnabled.description: Whether this vehicle's OWNER currently accepts ride requests against it (MYR-342) — the SAME value and the SAME semantics as VehicleSummary.rideShareEnabled, carried here so the owner's toggle can read its own current position from the detail surface it lives on. TRUE is the ordinary state and the state every vehicle starts in; FALSE means the owner has PAUSED ride requests for this vehicle, and the server refuses both new ride requests against it and accepts of outstanding ones with 409 `vehicle_unavailable` ('Ride sharing is paused for this vehicle'), for SCHEDULED rides as well as instant ones (a deliberate deviation from the in-service/offline reservation exemption — see the VehicleSummary sibling and rest-api.md §7.8). Set and cleared ONLY by the owner via `PUT /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/ride-share`; no vehicle state and no timer ever changes it. OPTIONAL AND TOLERANT: ABSENT means the server predates contracts v0.20.0 and MUST be read as ENABLED (true) — absence NEVER means paused. Visible to BOTH roles: viewers see it in the snapshot exactly as they see it in the catalog row, because a rider needs to know the shared car is not taking requests. Delivery: NOT STREAMED — a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER carries rideShareEnabled, so it is snapshot/list-read-only and refreshes on the next REST read or from the echo the PUT returns. Classified P0: an owner's availability switch on their own car, the same tier as the sibling `status`.

teslaAccessType.description: WHETHER THE ACCOUNT THAT LINKED THIS CAR OWNS IT ON TESLA'S SIDE OR MERELY DRIVES IT (MYR-599, contracts v0.39.0) — the SAME value and the SAME semantics as VehicleSummary.teslaAccessType, carried here so the detail surface and the catalog row can never disagree about one vehicle. Read that field for the full contract. In short: 'owner' is the ordinary case and the only case that existed before v0.39.0; 'driver' means the linker holds DRIVER access on somebody else's Tesla account, which is why such a car is provisioned behind an explicit owner-approval acknowledgment (`setupState.state` = 'awaiting_owner_acknowledgment', cleared by `POST /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/acknowledge-owner-approval`). WHAT IT IS FOR: the Settings / picker copy 'You drive this car', and knowing to offer the acknowledgment sheet even AFTER `setupState` has gone null. OPTIONAL AND TOLERANT: an ABSENT key means a server predating v0.39.0 and MUST be read as 'owner' — absence is a positive 'owner' by construction, not 'unknown', because a pre-v0.39.0 server provisioned owner-access cars only. An UNRECOGNISED value MUST be read as 'owner' too: never paint driver copy from a value the client does not know. RBAC: BOTH roles. Delivery: REST-READ-TIME ONLY, exactly like the siblings `setupState` and `rideShareEnabled` — a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER carries teslaAccessType — so it refreshes on the next GET /api/vehicles or /snapshot. P0: an operational fact about how the car reached the platform, carrying no VIN, no coordinate, no credential and no user content.

setupState.description: What is still standing between this vehicle and live telemetry, or NULL when there is nothing to say (MYR-491, contracts v0.24.0). OPTIONAL AND TOLERANT: an ABSENT key means the server predates v0.24.0 and MUST be read exactly like null — no card, no badge, no degraded rendering. THE FIELD NAMES ONE ACTION, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT: MYR-503's new owner met a dead Lock button because nothing told him his virtual key was never paired, and the client's explicit direction was that pairing guidance must NOT hang off a failed control ('does this make sense to the end user to have retry associated with lock?' — no). Consumers render this as a vehicle-level card BEFORE any command is attempted. NULL IS NOT 'READY': there is deliberately no `ready` member. Null means the server makes NO CLAIM — which covers a healthy streaming car, a car nobody has examined yet, and an expired claim — so a consumer MUST NOT paint a positive 'set up ✓' state from it. SERVER-DERIVED, EXACTLY ONCE: the value comes from the Go-owned `go_fleet_config_attempts` row (migrations 0031 + 0036) read together with `status` and `lastUpdated`, in a single server-side function that BOTH this snapshot and the VehicleSummary catalog row call. Consumers MUST NOT re-derive it, and are guaranteed the list row and the snapshot for one vehicle can never disagree. HONESTY RULES the server guarantees, worth knowing because they bound what the copy may say: (1) absence of evidence yields null — a vehicle with no schedule row never carries a state; (2) `configuring` EXPIRES after 24 hours of its evidence, falling back to null rather than to `awaiting_virtual_key`, because a car whose pairing has been proven is not awaiting a key; (3) a car that is currently STREAMING never carries `configuring` or `token_failed`, so a stale schedule row cannot put a setup card on a live car; (4) a car that streamed once and later went quiet is the FRESHNESS story (`lastUpdated`), not a setup state, and is deliberately excluded. NOT derived from `key_not_paired` command rejections: that error code is overloaded — the server returns it when ITS OWN signing proxy is unconfigured — so it cannot distinguish an unpaired owner from a broken deployment. DELIVERY: REST-READ-TIME ONLY, like the siblings `rideShareEnabled` and `serviceEstimatedEndAt` — a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER carries setupState, and by construction a vehicle in any of these states is not sending frames to attach it to. It refreshes on the next GET /api/vehicles or /snapshot. RBAC: BOTH roles — P0 operational state about the car, the same tier as the sibling `status` it qualifies, carrying no VIN, no coordinate, no credential and no user content. The viewer needs it for the strongest version of the usual argument: MYR-437's rider-side picker currently calls a never-streamed shared car 'offline' forever, and 'still being set up' is the true word for it.

state.description: Which setup condition holds. `awaiting_owner_acknowledgment` (MYR-599, contracts v0.39.0) — this car was linked by someone who holds DRIVER access on Tesla's side; the platform will not configure telemetry until that person acknowledges the owner approved it. `since` = when the driver-access row was recorded. THE LINKER MUST ACT: confirm the owner approved adding this car, via `POST /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/acknowledge-owner-approval` (vehicle-setup-completion.schema.json#/$defs/AcknowledgeOwnerApprovalRequest). IT SORTS FIRST — before `owner_access_required` / `awaiting_virtual_key` / `configuring` / `token_failed` — because consent precedes both pairing evidence and any push, and a car in this state has had NO config push attempted, so none of the others could truthfully apply to it. Read it together with the sibling `teslaAccessType`, which stays 'driver' for the life of the row after this state clears. `owner_access_required` (MYR-599, contracts v0.40.0) — Tesla REFUSED to create this car's fleet-telemetry config because the account that linked it holds DRIVER access, and Tesla's Fleet API lets ONLY the vehicle's OWNER account create one. `since` = when that refusal was observed. THE LINKER CANNOT FIX IT BY RECONNECTING, and copy MUST NOT say 'reconnect Tesla' — that is `token_failed`'s action, and here it would send a person round a loop that cannot end. The honest action is the only one that works: the car's Tesla OWNER adds the car in MyRoboTaxi under their OWN account and shares it with the driver. WHY IT CAN BE TRUSTED: Tesla's config POST answers a generic 404 `<VIN> not_found` for a driver token while THAT SAME TOKEN still lists the car, and a revoked grant answers the same 404 — so the server emits this member ONLY on positive evidence (the car carries a driver-access row, the owner-approval acknowledgment IS recorded, and the config POST 404'd while the vehicle list still contained the VIN) and NEVER from a bare 404. IT SORTS AFTER `awaiting_owner_acknowledgment` — the only state it can follow, because the refusal is observable only on a push and no push is attempted before consent is on record — and BEFORE `awaiting_virtual_key` / `configuring` / `token_failed`: a car in this state has an acknowledgment recorded and a push Tesla answered definitively, so 'waiting for the car' would be a fabricated progress state. UPSTREAM, AND NOT NECESSARILY PERMANENT: Tesla staff called DRIVER-token config POST 'coming soon' on teslamotors/fleet-telemetry#116 and #126 (2024-03-14), and as of 2026-09-05 no announcement says it shipped; if it does, the server's next push simply succeeds and this state clears on its own, with no consumer change. The sibling `teslaAccessType` stays 'driver' either way. `awaiting_virtual_key` — Tesla refused to apply this car's telemetry config because the owner's virtual key is not enrolled on the vehicle (Tesla's own `missing_key`/`not_paired` skip reason). THE OWNER MUST ACT: pair the key at the Tesla app deep link; nothing the server does heals this, and every signed command against the car will be rejected until it is done. `configuring` — the configuration side is in hand and the server is waiting for the car to open its telemetry session, including after the MYR-489 forced re-push. NO OWNER ACTION IS REQUIRED; copy should say so, and may suggest waking the car's screen if the state persists. Note this member does NOT by itself assert that pairing was detected — it is also reached when the server has just issued the car a brand-new config — so copy asserting 'pairing detected' would overstate it. `token_failed` — the owner's Tesla authorization can no longer be resolved or refreshed, so neither config pushes nor commands can reach the car. THE OWNER MUST ACT: reconnect the Tesla account. New members may be added in a minor version; consumers MUST treat an unrecognised value as 'setup is incomplete, reason unknown' and MUST NOT fail the decode.

since.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant at which the evidence behind `state` was recorded — the failing attempt for `awaiting_virtual_key`/`token_failed`, the pairing epoch or forced re-push for `configuring`. It is DATA FOR THE COPY ('for 2 days', escalating emphasis as it ages), NOT an input a consumer is expected to re-derive `state` from. Never zero and never in the future: the server floors it at the read instant, so a client may subtract it from `now` without guarding for a negative or absurd age.

lastUpdated.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent telemetry update applied to this vehicle state.

navigation.description: Navigation state delivered as a single atomic unit. When any navigation field changes, the server accumulates all sibling nav fields within a 500ms debounce window (NFR-3.2) and delivers them together. When navigation is cancelled, ALL fields in this group are atomically cleared to null (FR-2.3). MYR-602: the whole group is withheld from a plain `viewer` (superseding MYR-435) and granted to `ride_member` and `trip_participant`. A masked-away field is NOT a nav clear: the all-or-nothing predicate below governs DELIVERY to a role that holds the group, not the mask itself.
consistency-predicates: If destinationLatitude is non-null, then destinationLongitude MUST also be non-null, and vice versa.
If originLatitude is non-null, then originLongitude MUST also be non-null, and vice versa.
If destinationName is non-null, then destinationLatitude, destinationLongitude, and navRouteCoordinates MUST also be non-null (NFR-3.3).
If any navigation field is null, ALL navigation fields MUST be null (atomic clear on nav cancel, FR-2.3).
etaMinutes and tripDistanceRemaining MAY be null independently during the 500ms accumulation window, but the DB snapshot MUST have all-or-nothing consistency.
navigation.nullability: All fields nullable. Null = no active navigation.

charge.description: Battery and charge state delivered together. When any charge field changes within the same Tesla 500ms vehicle-side bucket, sibling fields are included in the same vehicle_update message. v1 expands this group to four fields per MYR-11; live WS wiring for chargeState and timeToFull completed by MYR-40 on 2026-04-22; DB persistence for both completed by MYR-41 on 2026-04-25 (Prisma columns + Go writer applier + SELECT/UPDATE wiring).
consistency-predicates: chargeLevel and estimatedRange MUST both be present in the DB snapshot (NFR-3.5). They are non-nullable with default 0.

chargeState and timeToFull are nullable in steady state — null surfaces when the vehicle has never charged or when no charge frame has arrived yet. Consumers MUST tolerate null on both wire and REST /snapshot responses.

chargeLevel: 0 is context-dependent. With status == 'offline', the UI SHOULD interpret chargeLevel: 0 as 'unknown' (no telemetry received yet, DB default). With status == 'driving' or 'parked' (i.e., the vehicle is online), chargeLevel: 0 SHOULD be interpreted as 'critical' or 'empty battery'. See §2.2 of vehicle-state-schema.md.
charge.nullability: chargeLevel and estimatedRange are non-nullable (default 0 on initial vehicle creation). chargeState and timeToFull are nullable on both wire and REST /snapshot — the Prisma-owned Vehicle columns are String?/Float? (post-MYR-41) and steady-state null is the expected shape for vehicles that have never charged.

gps.description: GPS position and orientation delivered together. On initial connect before the first GPS fix, latitude and longitude may be 0 (DB default). MYR-602: the whole group, together with `speed`, `locationName` and `locationAddress`, is withheld from a plain `viewer` and granted to `ride_member` and `trip_participant` — see the schema root description.
consistency-predicates: latitude and longitude MUST always be present together (NFR-3.3).
heading MUST be present whenever latitude/longitude are present.
Values of 0,0 for latitude/longitude represent the DB default (no GPS fix yet), not a valid location.
gps.nullability: Non-nullable in DB (default 0). SDK consumers SHOULD treat 0,0 as 'no fix'.

gear.description: Gear position and derived vehicle status delivered together. When gearPosition changes, the server derives status (driving/parked) and includes both fields in the same message.
consistency-predicates: When gearPosition is 'D' or 'R', status MUST be 'driving'.
When gearPosition is 'P' or 'N', status MUST be 'parked' (unless overridden by charging/offline/in_service logic).
status is always present; gearPosition is nullable (null = vehicle asleep or gear not yet reported).
gear.nullability: gearPosition is nullable. status is non-nullable (default 'offline').
